newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude called lower in consolidation.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude called lower in consolidation.

text.p: NYMEX crude was called lower Friday amid a consolidation of the oil complex following two consecutive sessions of refined product-led rallies.
Crude was called 10 to 15 cents a barrel lower. Heating oil was called 0.50 to 0.75 cent a gallon lower while gasoline was called unchanged to 0.25 cent off a gallon.

"This is definitely consolidation. I think the short covering we saw in the refined products ahead of expiry should be pretty much done with now," said Refco Inc vice president Victor Yu. The February refined product contract expires Friday.
Dealers said gasoline's losses would be limited by a slew of refinery turnarounds diminishing output ahead of the spring and summer season when gasoline demand traditionally peaks.

On Thursday, March crude settled up 40 cents a barrel at $24.87. February heating oil finished up 1.50 cents at 70.34 cents a gallon while February gasoline ended up 1.59 cents a gallon at 69.82 cents.

Dealers noted open interest in the Feb heat contract declined Wednesday, indicating the rally was fueled by short covering in the expiring front month rather than new long positions entering the market.
On Wednesday, Feb heat open interest was down 6,150 lots to 15,156 lots.
Relatively tight prompt refined product supply has sparked concern of a short squeeze, but some dealers said that talk was overblown.
"From what I hear from industry sources, the stocks are not going to get that much lower than they are now," said one New York refined product dealer.
The American Petroleum Institute (API) said Tuesday that for the week ended January 24, distillate stocks, which are comprised of heating oil and diesel, dropped 2.85 million barrels.
Gasoline stocks grew 1.84 million barrels but the year over year shortfall steepened to 11.00 milion barrels from 9.35 million barrels the week earlier.
((-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761))
